questions.q: What is a span, as defined in this lesson?
options: A timed unit of work, created when it starts and closed when it finishes, carrying a name, attributes, and a parent reference
A log line written after a request finishes, summarizing what happened
A dashboard panel showing aggregate latency
A fixed-size buffer used to store metrics
questions.explain: A span wraps a real unit of work in time — it's created at the start of the operation and closed at the end, not reconstructed afterward from a log.

questions.q: What mechanical problem does trace context propagation actually solve?
options: It compresses trace data before writing it to disk
It encrypts span data for transit between services
It converts logs into metrics automatically
checkout-service and inventory-service are separate processes that don't share memory, so the trace ID and parent span ID must be passed across the network call itself, usually in a header
questions.explain: Since separate services don't share memory, the calling service has to inject the trace ID and its span ID into the outgoing request so the receiver's new span attaches to the correct trace.

questions.q: What happens when a service in the middle of a call chain fails to forward the traceparent header?
options: The request is automatically retried three times
The trace silently splits into two disconnected traces instead of throwing a visible error
The receiving service crashes immediately with a fatal error
Tracing is disabled platform-wide until the header is restored
questions.explain: A dropped traceparent header doesn't error loudly — it just breaks the connective tissue between hops, which is why broken propagation is easy to miss until you notice traces ending at a service boundary.

questions.q: In the OpenTelemetry model, what is the role of an Exporter?
options: It generates random trace IDs for new requests
It sets the log level for a service
It ships finished spans out of the process to a backend, such as Jaeger or Tempo, for storage and querying
It creates the required_providers block for a Terraform configuration
questions.explain: The Exporter is the piece of the OpenTelemetry model responsible for sending completed span data to wherever it will be stored and queried later.

questions.q: Why does sampling exist, and what's the cost of setting the sample rate too low?
options: Sampling only affects which log level is used, with no cost either way
Sampling exists purely for legal compliance and has no storage implications
Sampling guarantees every trace is captured regardless of the configured rate
Exporting a full trace for every request is often more data than it's worth storing; setting the rate too low risks never capturing the one trace needed for an obscure, intermittent bug
questions.explain: Sampling trades storage cost against coverage — keeping errors and slow outliers plus a random slice of everything else, while too low a rate risks missing the specific trace you'll need later.
